newsitem.title: USA: Wisconsin postpones 485 MW nuke restart.
newsitem.headline: Wisconsin postpones 485 MW nuke restart.

text.p: Wisconsin Electric Power Co postponed the restart of its 485 megawatt (MW) Point Beach 1 nuclear power unit and has no new date on which it is likely to resume production, a company spokeswoman said Wednesday.

Point Beach 1, located in Two Rivers, Wis., is currently being moved into a cold shutdown mode, postponing original plans which would have seen the unit resume power production today, said spokeswoman Jackie Olson.
The unit was taken off line Feb 18 to repair a cooling system pump. Previous plans to restart the unit were delayed for repairs to an emergency diesel generator.
"We do not have a restart date for unit 1 at this time," Olson said, adding "but we are going to be focusing our efforts on unit 2."
The adjacent 485 MW Point Beach nuclear unit 2 is expected to return to service in mid-April following a refueling outage that began in October, 1996.
Wisconsin Electric is a subsidiary of Wisconsin Energy Corp.
